findings.title: Date-override window check rejects valid slots and accepts partial overlaps
findings.body: checkIfIsAvailable treats a slot as outside the date override if it is outside any one override range on that calendar day. dateOverrides.find returns the first range for which the slot ends before the range start or starts after the range end, and the caller then returns false. With two ranges on the same day (for example 09:00-11:00 and 14:00-16:00), a slot fully inside the first range is still rejected because it is outside the second. The inverse is also wrong: a slot that only partially overlaps a range does not hit either outside-condition, so it is treated as inside. Fixed-host round-robin days with more than one override, or slots that stick out of the override, are therefore bookable or hidden incorrectly.

findings.title: All-day block comparison never matches
findings.body: The unavailable-all-day branch compares two Dayjs instances with ===. That checks object identity, not time, so dayjs(date.start).add(...) === dayjs(date.end).add(...) is always false. A date override stored with equal start and end (the usual all-day unavailable marker) never takes this path and depends on the other window checks, which do not treat a zero-length range as blocking the whole day.

findings.title: Override match returns available before busy times are checked
findings.body: If any date override exists on the slot's calendar day and the slot was not rejected by the window checks, checkIfIsAvailable returns true immediately. Busy calendar events, existing bookings, and buffers passed in busy are never consulted. A fixed host who set a date override can therefore be booked on top of a meeting that falls inside that override, which is a double-booking.

findings.title: Working-hours fallback treats days off and later ranges as available
findings.body: When no date override matches, availability is decided with workingHours.find that returns true (slot rejected) only when some entry both includes slotStartTime.day() and does not contain the slot start. If the weekday is absent from every entry, find returns undefined and the function falls through to the busy check and can return true, so a fixed host's day off is still bookable in round-robin. If several ranges share that weekday, the first range that does not contain the slot makes find succeed even when a later range does contain it, so a slot inside a second interval is rejected. end is also computed from the slot start minute, not slot start plus event length, so a meeting that starts inside hours and runs past workingHour.endTime is accepted.

findings.title: Override offset is reduced to clock time and can drop the range
findings.body: After shifting the override by inviteeUtcOffset - organizerUtcOffset, only .hour() and .minute() are kept. A shift across midnight is applied as minutes-on-the-same-invitee-day that passed the activeOverrides filter, so the window lands on the wrong clock time (and often the wrong date). If the end crosses midnight and the start does not, endTime becomes less than startTime and buildSlots skips the range with start >= end, so that date override disappears entirely for attendees in a timezone on the other side of midnight from the organizer.

findings.title: New test does not cover fixed-host overrides or a real timezone shift
findings.body: The added getSchedule call asks for Asia/Dhaka but expects the same UTC slot list already asserted for Asia/Kolkata, and it uses a personal event with no hosts. It cannot fail if fixed-host date overrides are ignored in round-robin, if an override day still ignores busy time, or if the offset math moves slots across a date boundary. The PR's stated fixes (#8207 / fixed hosts, timezone-adjusted overrides) ship with no assertion that would catch the checkIfIsAvailable regressions.
